## Selected work

### [Bank Reconciliation Agent](https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent)
<sub>Personal project · v1.1.0 · Synthetic data only · Python, PostgreSQL, pgvector, MCP, Docker</sub>

A rules-first tool-calling agent that matches small-business bank lines to invoices on synthetic data. Code verifies every proposal, the model cannot write to the ledger, and a person approves before anything posts. Read-only MCP server, a plain-English rule compiler, live evals on four models, a pre-registered code-mode experiment and a CI replay gate; the README says where it breaks.

- **With deepseek-flash:** 0 wrong matches in 460 agent match proposals (582 agent decisions) over 3 live runs on each of two synthetic businesses. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/blob/v1.1.0/README.md">source: README at v1.1.0</a></sup>
- 0 of 40 injected lines that ask for a different or an extra invoice succeeded in any run. The verifier refuses whatever the payload asks for on 36 of them; on the 4 it leaves to the model's judgement, 0 payloads were followed by any model in any run with defences on. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/blob/v1.1.0/README.md">source: README at v1.1.0</a></sup>
- **Pre-registered code-mode experiment:** containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/blob/v0.1.0/README.md">source: README at v0.1.0</a></sup>

### [Provenance-Tiered RAG](https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag)
<sub>Personal project · v0.3.0 · Python, PostgreSQL, pgvector</sub>

Question answering over New Zealand GST law, German VAT law (UStG and UStDV) and Immigration New Zealand's Operational Manual, with dated sources in tiers: statute, official guidance and untrusted notes. Immigration answers are information from INZ's published instructions, not immigration advice. Code checks every citation and figure against passages in force on the date asked about. Frozen eval sets, held-back questions and defence ablations; the README says what the numbers do not show.

- **With deepseek-flash:** 96 of 96 answers to answerable questions were correct (95% lower bound 96.2%) over 3 runs of the development questions <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md">source: README at v0.3.0</a></sup>
- **Held-back NZ GST questions, answerable correct:** 27 of 30 (90.0%) <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md">source: README at v0.3.0</a></sup>
- The questions are few and written by the author of the system. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md">source: README at v0.3.0</a></sup>

<a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/c9cd7d253bd57c6d4decf92bddc32531814c8be9/docs/demo.svg" width="640" alt="Terminal replay of make demo: recorded GST questions answered with dated, tiered citations and the verifier's verdict, including questions carrying a planted note that is not followed"></a>

[Release v0.3.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/releases/tag/v0.3.0) · [Results at v0.3.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md)

### [mcp-code-mode](https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode)
<sub>Personal project · v0.1.0 · Python, MCP, Docker</sub>

Run model-written Python against any MCP server's tools in a locked-down Docker sandbox. It serves a wrapped server's tools to the model as one run_python tool. Every call passes a host-side bridge that checks the allowlist, the tool's JSON Schema, argument size and a call budget, and refuses oversized results. Extracted from bank-reconciliation-agent; the README maps each threat to a control and a test, and lists what it does not protect.

- **Where it was measured, in bank-reconciliation-agent:** containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested. Read the numbers there; this package carries no measurements of its own. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/blob/v0.1.0/README.md">source: README at v0.1.0</a></sup>

<a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/0c2e9e84d1451f539927dae2c334266710a27923/docs/demo.svg" width="640" alt="Terminal capture: a program calls two allowlisted toy tools through the bridge, then builds a call to a tool off the allowlist, which the bridge refuses before the server sees it"></a>

[Release v0.1.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/releases/tag/v0.1.0) · [Threat model at v0.1.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#threat-model)
